idiom_name: trait + Box<dyn UserDao> returned by a match over a configuration value
implementation_notes: Rust has no inheritance, so the DAO interface is a trait and the factory is an ordinary function, or an enum dispatch, that matches a configuration value and returns Box<dyn UserDao> (or a concrete generic when the store is fixed at compile time); trait objects replace the abstract factory's polymorphic creation, and an enum is cheaper when the store set is closed. The classic structure is worth its dynamic dispatch only when stores are open-ended (plugins); with a fixed set, generics or an enum keep DAO calls monomorphised. The pool is created once at the composition root and passed down, never built per DAO.
pitfalls: A DAO behind Box<dyn UserDao> must carry the bounds it needs (Send + Sync) to be shared across tasks; omitting them compiles until the DAO meets a multi-threaded runtime.
Trait objects require object-safe methods: generic or async methods force enum dispatch, a boxed future (Pin<Box<dyn Future>>) or the async-trait crate - a real design fork.
Pools are cheap to clone but expensive to create: pass one pool from main or the composition root instead of constructing one per DAO.

variants.name: sqlx::Any runtime-generic driver
variants.implementation_notes: sqlx's any module is a genuine store-selection mechanism in the library: call install_default_drivers() once, then AnyPool::connect takes a DSN whose scheme selects the compiled-in driver at runtime and every query becomes store-agnostic. It supplies the store half of the pattern - the driver registry by URL scheme - while the DAO traits and their SQL stay hand-written; choose it when one binary must support several backends and the SQL is common enough, and skip it when dialect-specific SQL or driver-specific row types matter more than coverage.
pitfalls: install_default_drivers() must run before any Any connection; using AnyConnection or AnyPool without it panics, as the crate documentation states.
AnyConnection erases driver-specific types, so features relying on them (custom enums, some numeric handling) need casting or per-driver DAO paths.
